description:
We're building an interactive space mission design game where players become mission planners, customize spacecraft, select equipment, manage resources, and explore space through simulated missions.

We're looking for creative and motivated teammates interested in web/game development, UI/UX, space science, astronomy, or 3D design.

If you love space exploration, problem-solving, and turning creative ideas into reality, join us!
summary:
MISSION FORGE: Design. Decide. Simulate. Discover.

MISSION FORGE is an interactive, educational space mission design and simulation game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on experience.

Players take on the role of space mission directors, designing and managing scientific missions from initial objectives to final operations. They make real-world-inspired decisions about spacecraft architecture, propulsion, scientific instruments, orbital trajectories, power systems, communications, budgets, and mission risks.

Unlike traditional space games focused on arcade challenges, MISSION FORGE emphasizes strategic thinking, scientific reasoning, and engineering trade-offs. Players experience realistic mission scenarios, respond to unexpected operational challenges, analyze simulated scientific data, and evaluate mission performance.

By incorporating NASA mission design principles, relevant NASA resources, and interactive visualizations, the platform makes space exploration and systems engineering more accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Its progressive learning modes support beginners while offering increasingly challenging experiences for advanced users.

MISSION FORGE aims to turn learning about space missions into an immersive experience where every decision matters and every mission becomes an opportunity to discover.
details:
MISSION FORGE – STARBOUND EDITION is an interactive space mission design game that helps players understand how real space missions are planned and the engineering decisions behind them.

Designing a space mission involves balancing several challenges, including spacecraft mass, scientific instruments, power, propulsion, communication, launch vehicle capacity, and mission cost. Our project turns these complex decisions into an interactive learning experience.

Players choose a scientific mission, build and configure their spacecraft, select instruments and technical systems, and check whether their design meets the mission requirements. They then launch their spacecraft and face simulated mission events where their decisions can affect mission performance, reliability, and scientific results.

The game provides feedback, performance scores, and a final mission report to help players understand the consequences of their choices and learn from both successful and unsuccessful designs.

Our goal is to make space mission engineering more accessible and engaging, allowing students and space enthusiasts to explore the challenges of spacecraft design through hands-on experimentation.
